entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Registered through the api.account module listed in ROUTES in app.py.

stores.name: users

fields.name: metadata_json
fields.note: A comment on the column says the client sets arbitrary key/value pairs and that support pastes contact details into it.

erasure.note: anonymize_user writes only email and full_name, so this column keeps whatever the client and support wrote into it.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: The application's own state column for the row.

erasure.note: No code in the repository assigns deleted_at, and the row is never deleted.
close_account overwrites email with its SHA-256 hash and full_name with the constant "removed"; the row and its primary key stay, and the hashed email still points at the same person.

stores.note: Table holding the account holder record.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: notes
fields.note: A comment on the column says the free text may contain phone numbers.

erasure.note: close_account touches only two columns on the user row and deletes nothing, and the User.tickets relationship carries no cascade argument, so ticket rows stay with their text and their user_id.

stores.note: Table holding support tickets, linked to the user by user_id.

stores.name: request_log

fields.name: ip_address
fields.note: Read from request.client.host and written to the log line at middleware.py:11.

erasure.note: No code reads or removes anything from this logger, and close_account only writes to the user row.

stores.note: Standard-library logger that records the caller's IP address and the request path for every request.

missing_entry_points.name: anonymize_user
missing_entry_points.expected: declare anonymize_user as an entry point, or say in its note why it is not one
